propositions: Bridge git delivery abandons after a single transient transport failure (TLS/DNS/timeout) instead of retrying, losing converged work with unpushed commits
The push.py retry logic only retries genuine non-fast-forward conflicts, treating all other push failures as terminal, conflating permanent policy violations with retriable transport faults

Transport-retriable failures (certificate verification, connection reset, timeout, promisor fetch failures) must be distinguished from terminal policy declines using a subtractive classifier similar to existing _is_non_fast_forward and _ref_lock patterns

Both the explicit fetch in merge recovery and the on-demand promisor fetch during merge operations fail with transport faults and need unified retry handling with bounded backoff (3 attempts total: 0.5s, 2.0s delays)
Policy-decline failures must remain strictly terminal with one attempt, while transport failures retry with backoff and eventually raise with same reason vocabulary and unpushed-commit summary
